The Peaceful dove Geopelia placida is a small, granivorous columbid native to northern and eastern Australia, where it inhabits open woodlands and grassy margins. Field-based measurements indicate that newly hatched chicks emerge from the egg at a remarkably low wet weight of only 3.35 grams [Ww0 = 3.35 grams], a value that underscores the altricial state of development characteristic of many doves. The incubation period, which in this species is recorded at 13.5 days [ab = 13.5 days] when eggs are maintained at a constant temperature of 39 °C [T = 39 °C], is comparable to that of other small-bodied members of the genus Geopelia. This relatively brief embryonic phase is followed by a rapid growth trajectory, a necessary adaptation for offspring that must reach independence within a single breeding season. The initial mass of the neonate is modest even by columbid standards, suggesting that the yolk reserves of the egg are concentrated toward sustaining a short, intensive developmental window rather than supporting a more prolonged period of provisioning within the nest.

As the nestling progresses through its early development, a key milestone is the achievement of fledging, when the young bird attains sufficient wing strength and feather development for sustained flight. Under the warm thermal conditions typical of the species' active metabolic periods, at a body temperature of 40.5 °C [T = 40.5 °C], this transition to independence occurs approximately 16 days after hatching [tx = approximately 16 days after hatching] and, later, gonadal activation marks puberty, which is reached at 48 days since birth [tp = 48 days since birth]. This comparatively short nestling period aligns with the life history strategy of many tropical and subtropical columbids, where rapid development is favored to minimize the risk of nest predation. During this nest-dependent phase, the chick is brooded and provisioned almost exclusively by both parents, a biparental care system that facilitates the high feeding rates required to sustain such swift growth. Following fledging, the young bird remains within the natal territory for several weeks before dispersing, gradually refining its foraging skills on a diet of small seeds and occasional invertebrates.

Reproduction in this species is characterized by a modest reproductive output distributed across the calendar year. Females typically lay two eggs per clutch [N_R_i = two eggs per clutch] and produce approximately one clutch per year [F_R_i = approximately one clutch per year], a relatively low annual fecundity compared to many small passerines but typical of the slow-paced life history strategy seen in doves. Under the species' habitual body temperature of 40.5 °C [T = 40.5 °C], the age at which a female produces her first successful brood has been recorded at 511 days since birth [tR = 511 days since birth], a delay that reflects the investment in pair bonding and territory acquisition that precedes nesting in these monogamous birds. This extended interval between maturation and first reproduction is an important demographic parameter, as it influences the generation time of the population and its capacity to recover from environmental perturbations.

Physiological studies of the Peaceful dove have revealed a basal metabolic rate that is consistent with its body size and sedentary lifestyle. Under the species' habitual body temperature of 40.5 °C [T = 40.5 °C], respirometry trials have recorded a maximum resting oxygen consumption of 64 milliliters per hour [JOi = 64 milliliters per hour], a value that supports the species' low-energy foraging strategy. In terms of ultimate body size, adult females generally reach a maximum wet weight of 45 grams [Wwi = 45 grams], whereas males are somewhat heavier, attaining up to 49.4 grams [Wwi = up to 49.4 grams]. This slight sexual dimorphism in mass may relate to the male's role in nest defense and courtship feeding. Maximum recorded longevity in the species has been estimated at 5,694 days [am = 5,694 days] under the same thermal regime, placing the Peaceful dove among the longer-lived columbids for its body size at a temperature of 40.5 °C [T = 40.5 °C].
